header.provenance: own-binary-via-Ghidra (function entry points + RTTI vtable map) + objdump -d -M intel over .text of the same sha256-pinned file
header.status: LEADS, NOT FACTS. Every row carries the instruction address that produced it. Per project rule a number enters a layout header or the manifest only after that instruction has been read back and cited in the header itself. Nothing here is a confirmed fact.
header.what_this_is: `PUSH <n>; CALL operator new (0x7C8E17)` immediately before a constructor call gives the object's exact size. Each row binds one constructor to the size pushed at its allocation sites, and to the RTTI class name of the vtable that constructor stores at offset 0.
method: every direct CALL to 0x7C8E17 in .text is an allocation site;
the single argument is the last PUSH before that call (immediate only; a PUSH of a register is a computed size and the site is dropped);
the returned pointer is followed forward through register and frame-slot moves until a CALL is reached with that pointer in ECX -- that callee is the constructor;
sites disagreeing on the size are reported in conflicting_sizes and the majority value is taken (unanimous=false).

field_notes.closes: false means the constructor writes at or beyond the allocated size -- either the size binding or the receiver tracking is wrong for that row, so read it by hand.
field_notes.unanimous: every allocation site pushed the same size.

classes.size_caveat: this constructor is also called from another constructor, so it is a base-class ctor; an allocation site that calls it directly is allocating a DERIVED object whose own ctor was inlined, and the size belongs to that derived class, not to this one
